title: No sign-in, claim, session or API-token flow for authenticated mode; credential carriage is undefined
evidence: docs/design.md:323-325 promises `authenticated` mode with a one-time claim URL and design.md:327 `FLEET_TOKEN` for scripts; status.proto:221 defines PRINCIPAL_KIND_API_TOKEN. But service.proto (all 189 lines) has no claim/login/logout/token RPC; 02b-hub-api.md:224-225 defers 'API tokens and user management' as an open question; 02b never mentions auth_mode at all (grep local_trusted/authenticated hits only design.md, common.proto:165-168, 04-technology-review.md:214). GetServerInfoResponse.caller is 'unset when not signed in' (common.proto:167-168) but nothing says how someone becomes signed in. 02b:204 lists UNAUTHENTICATED with no reason code. ADR 0016 (WebSocket attach) and 02b:176 never say whether credentials are a cookie, a bearer header, or a signed request.
problem: A React dashboard in authenticated mode cannot be built: there is no way to claim the first-admin URL, log in, hold a session across Connect unary + Watch stream + WebSocket attach, log out, or mint a CLI token. Browsers cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket, so the carrier choice (HttpOnly cookie vs token) changes the UI, CLI and Watch/attach handlers. There is also no User resource: Principal.id, Role assignment and `Device.principal_id` (device.proto:32) reference users the API cannot create or list.
fix: Add a short 'Authentication' section to 02b. It should say where the claim is handled (a fleetd command or plain HTTP, not FleetService) and how credentials are carried: browser = HttpOnly SameSite session cookie, which also covers the same-origin WebSocket upgrade; CLI/scripts = Authorization bearer token from FLEET_TOKEN. Keep token and user RPCs deferred under open question 1 (v3). Do not add an AuthService or new reason codes now.
verify: The gap is real but the severity is overstated. Confirmed: service.proto has no claim/login/logout/token RPC; design.md:323-327 promises the claim URL and FLEET_TOKEN; 02b has no auth section and never says how credentials ride Connect, Watch or the attach WebSocket (grep for cookie, bearer, ticket and Origin finds nothing in docs or api). However 02b:224-225 and ADR 0018:128 already list 'API tokens and user management as RPCs, or fleetd commands only' as an open question. design.md:425-439 puts login and browser attach in v3, and v1/v2 run on local_trusted. The first-admin claim can be a plain HTTP endpoint or fleetd command outside FleetService, so no proto change blocks v1/v2. Any RPCs are additive. The part that does matter now (principal and Origin rules in local_trusted) is covered under local-trusted-attack-surface.
resolution: New 02f-hub-authentication.md and hub/v1/auth.proto, token.proto: claim URL (first owner invite, fragment token, RedeemInvite), passkey Begin/Finish registration and login (WebAuthn JSON), GitHub sign-in as two redirect endpoints with a users-based allow-list, login sessions with an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, SignOut, Users and invites, API tokens (create once-shown, list, revoke); credential carriers per transport; GetServerInfo gains sign_in_methods and claim_pending; 17 RPCs added to service.proto; ADR 0019 addendum 10 to 12.

title: Roles and scopes are mixed: what Role does a narrowed device or token send to the agent, and which check wins?
evidence: Agent re-checks `requested_by.role` against command class and kind (02-contracts.md:186-187, 409, 416; command_goal.proto:160,189). Principal.role (status.proto:235) exists for every Principal; for kind DEVICE/API_TOKEN 02b:166 says only 'at most its user's scopes'. Role-based rules still appear in the hub API: KillWindowRequest 'needs ROLE_OWNER and an approval' (session.proto:245-246) while service.proto:76 labels KillWindow [SESSIONS_WRITE]; `Approval.required_role` (triage.proto:192-193) says 'Lowest role or scope' but the type is Role; PruneWorktree allow_dirty needs ROLE_OWNER (02-contracts.md:373 of 03c, 02-contracts.md:454).
problem: If the hub fills requested_by.role from on_behalf_of (the owner) a phone granted only SESSIONS_WRITE passes the agent's owner-only checks (developer KillWindow, allow_dirty), so narrowed scopes do not narrow what the agent allows. If it fills a lower role, there is no role for 'operator minus APPROVALS'. Approval.required_role cannot express a scope. Roles are documented as 'never compared numerically' but required_role/ROLE_OWNER are exactly role comparisons.
fix: Document in 02b that the hub sets requested_by.role to the highest role whose scope set is a subset of the caller's effective scopes. OWNER requires ADMIN, SETTINGS, APPROVALS and SESSIONS_WRITE, so a narrowed device or token is never OWNER. Reconcile KillWindow's label with its message comment (for example 'SESSIONS_WRITE, and a developer's window also needs an owner-level principal and an approval'). Fix the required_role comment to name roles only, or add `required_scope` as a new field and reserve nothing. Changing the field is unnecessary because it is additive.
verify: Confirmed. The agent re-checks requested_by.role against command class and kind (02-contracts.md:186-187, 409; command_goal.proto:160,189), and 02-contracts.md:454 requires ROLE_OWNER for KillWindow on a developer window and for allow_dirty. 02-contracts.md:336-343 and 02b:166 say a device or token acts on_behalf_of the owner with 'at most its user's scopes' but never say what Principal.role the hub sends for a narrowed DEVICE or API_TOKEN. If it copies the owner's role, narrowed scopes do not narrow the agent's checks. service.proto:76 labels KillWindow [SESSIONS_WRITE] while session.proto:245-246 says it needs ROLE_OWNER and an approval. triage.proto:192-193 says 'Lowest role or scope' but the field is a Role. The agent's role check is only 'defense in depth' (02-contracts.md:416-418), so the main enforcement is hub-side scopes, which makes this a doc and consistency gap rather than a wire blocker.
resolution: 02d "Role sent to the agent": the hub sends the narrowest role covering the effective scopes, OWNER only with SESSIONS_WRITE, APPROVALS, SETTINGS and ADMIN, so a narrowed device or token is never OWNER; hub scope check and agent role check both apply, stricter wins. Principal.role, KillWindowRequest and Approval.required_role comments reconciled (required_role is a role covered by the decider's mapped role).

title: local_trusted mode and WebSocket attach: no Origin/Host rules, no attach ticket, principal and auth_mode type undefined
evidence: design.md:323 `local_trusted` = hub on localhost, no login; ADR 0016:34 and 04-technology-review.md:237 define terminal attach as a WebSocket with input (terminal.proto:44-55 `bytes input`) but nothing specifies how it authenticates or checks Origin. 02b never mentions local_trusted, and design.md:318 says the hub listens only on the Tailscale interface and 'Browser terminal attach requires login', which contradicts local_trusted-on-localhost without a stated exception. GetServerInfoResponse.auth_mode is `string` (common.proto:165-166). No statement of which Principal (id, role, kind) a request has in local_trusted mode, though audit, Operation.requested_by, FLEET_OWNER and idempotency scoping (02b:69-70) all need a Principal.id.
problem: With no login, any web page the owner visits can open ws://localhost:<port> (WebSockets are not subject to CORS) or use DNS rebinding and type into the owner's tmux sessions and answer approvals: cross-site WebSocket hijacking is the main real-world attack on exactly this design. In authenticated mode the same applies to a cookie without CSRF/Origin checks. auth_mode as a free string will be wire-incompatible to change to an enum later.
fix: Document in 02b: local_trusted binds loopback only and refuses non-loopback addresses; every request and WebSocket upgrade passes a Host allow-list and same-origin Origin check; the fixed local principal is {id: "local-owner", kind USER, role OWNER}; attach in local_trusted follows the same Origin rule and design.md:318 is reconciled to 'login required in authenticated mode'. Change `auth_mode` to an enum (LOCAL_TRUSTED, AUTHENTICATED) before codegen. A CreateAttachTicket RPC is optional and can wait for v3.
verify: Confirmed. design.md:318-319 says the hub listens only on the Tailscale interface and browser attach requires login, while design.md:323-325 defines local_trusted as localhost with no login. 04-technology-review.md:214 contemplates plain-HTTP localhost and the attach WebSocket (ADR 0016:31-33) is specified without any authentication, Origin or Host check. common.proto:165-166 types auth_mode as a free `string`. The Principal used in local_trusted (audit, requested_by, FLEET_OWNER, idempotency scope at 02b:69-70) is never defined. Cross-site WebSocket hijacking and DNS rebinding are the standard attacks on a no-login localhost control plane that can type into tmux and answer approvals. In v2 the same applies to unary Connect calls that dispatch goals. Attach itself is v3 (design.md:439), but the Origin/Host rules and principal are needed for any v1 server. The string-to-enum change is wire-incompatible, so it is cheapest before codegen.
resolution: local_trusted binds loopback only and refuses other addresses; fixed principal local-owner (kind USER, role OWNER); Host allow-list, Origin check and no-CORS rules on every transport (02f); new HOST_NOT_ALLOWED and ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED reasons; CreateAttachTicket makes attach a second lock; AuthMode comments in common.proto; design.md reconciled to authenticated mode. (auth_mode was already an enum from theme A.)

title: No Role x CommandClass x kind matrix, so what the hub's own SCHEDULER principal may do on the agent is undefined
evidence: 01b-harness-commands.md:35-42 gives per-class rules only in terms of 'operator role' and 'local approval or explicit owner action'; status.proto:199-210 says roles are permission sets, SCHEDULER is a separate Role; 02b-hub-api.md:154 says SCHEDULER appears as requested_by. The agent re-checks role per kind/class (02-contracts.md envelope checks, ROLE_INSUFFICIENT). The scheduler-issued paths include: StartGoal with GoalSpec.model/effort typed as SESSION-class /model and /effort (command_goal.proto:56-60, 01b:38), fresh_context typing DESTRUCTIVE /clear (command_goal.proto:61-65), nudge SendKeys and RespawnPane 'dangerous kind; may need local approval' (03c-goals.md:290-296, :370 LOCAL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT -> STUCK), reserve-line /goal pause (03b-usage-and-sync.md:102-104), LIMIT_WAIT resume (02-contracts.md:361-366), PruneWorktree/KillWindow after merged_grace (03c-goals.md:311-316).
problem: Implementers of the agent's check and of the scheduler cannot tell whether an unattended auto-dispatch with model/effort/fresh_context is allowed, whether every auto-recovery respawn needs a person at the machine, or whether a viewer-vs-scheduler comparison is even meaningful.
fix: Add a Role x command kind/class table (VIEWER, OPERATOR, OWNER, SCHEDULER, ARBITER, with default AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM) to 02-contracts.md and the policy defaults. Recommend SCHEDULER may issue StartGoal (incl. model/effort), nudge SendKeys, GOAL and OBSERVE harness commands, Interrupt, SetSessionAvailability, probe commands, PruneWorktree and fleet-window KillWindow, with fresh_context and RespawnPane allowed only in fleet-started sessions. No proto change.
verify: Confirmed. The agent re-checks role against command class (02-contracts.md:186-188, status.proto:199-210), but 01b-harness-commands.md:35-42 phrases the classes in terms of 'operator role' and 'local approval or explicit owner action', and a repo-wide grep finds no matrix covering ROLE_SCHEDULER on the agent. The only scope table (02b-hub-api.md:~150-160) is for hub API callers and says SCHEDULER/ARBITER never call that API. SCHEDULER-issued paths include GoalSpec.model/effort (SESSION class), fresh_context (/clear, DESTRUCTIVE, command_goal.proto:56-65), nudge SendKeys and RespawnPane (03c:290-296, 'may need local approval'), and PruneWorktree/KillWindow (03c:311-316). ADR 0004:121 and :385 make local approval for dangerous kinds configurable, but they do not say what the scheduler may do unattended. Without it the agent role check and the scheduler's auto-recovery cannot be implemented consistently.
resolution: 02g-agent-security.md has the Role x command kind/class matrix (VIEWER, OPERATOR, OWNER, SCHEDULER, ARBITER; A, L, L!, F, -), with the scheduler allowed unattended StartGoal (incl. model and effort), nudges, Interrupt, probes, PruneWorktree and fleet-window KillWindow, fresh_context and RespawnPane only in fleet-started sessions; command.proto requested_by comment points to it. No wire change.

title: Enroll/Connect-level failures (token reasons, fleet mismatch, unknown machine) have no typed representation
evidence: 03-workflows.md:184 says Enroll 'fails with a gRPC error naming the reason' (expired, used) and the agent prints it, but ReasonCode (status.proto:72-168) has no token/enroll codes; ErrorDetail on a unary RPC error is only defined for the hub API (status.proto:155-185). EnrollResponse.fleet_id (agent.proto:85-87) says an agent 'refuses a hub with another fleet_id', yet HelloAck (agent.proto:170-198) has no fleet_id, so the check can only ever run at enroll. ByeReason (agent.proto:264-280) has no 'unknown machine' (hub store recreated with the CA kept, a case 03-workflows.md:325 only half covers: REVOKED forces a new token and loses previous_machine_id history) and no fleet mismatch. 03-workflows.md:264-269 treats any second Hello with a live stream as duplicate identity and raises a triage warning, but a sleeping laptop or restarted agent routinely reconnects while the hub still holds the old half-open stream (new boot_id, same install_id), which is indistinguishable from a cloned state dir that has the same install_id (agent.proto:59-63).
problem: Enroll error classes, fleet-id check at connect, and an unknown-machine path are unspecified; duplicate-identity detection will page the owner on benign reconnects.
fix: Specify the unknown-machine path (Bye with a new UNKNOWN_MACHINE reason, agent re-enrolls with previous_machine_id). Define duplicate identity as an old stream with a Heartbeat within 45 s when the new Hello arrives; otherwise silent takeover with no triage. Typed Enroll error codes and HelloAck.fleet_id are optional.
verify: Mostly speculative; one real piece. Enroll errors as a gRPC status naming the reason (03-workflows.md:184) are adequate for the CLI that prints and exits, so typed ReasonCodes are optional, and fleet mismatch at connect is largely covered by mTLS against the pinned CA. Real and unspecified: (a) a Hello from a machine_id the hub does not know (store recreated with the CA kept) has no defined behavior or ByeReason (grep for unknown machine finds nothing; 03-workflows.md:149 only has REVOKED); (b) 03-workflows.md:264-269 raises a triage warning on every duplicate-identity displacement, though a sleeping laptop or restarted agent routinely reconnects while the hub still holds the old half-open stream (STALE at 45 s, OFFLINE at 3 min), so benign reconnects would page the owner; only repeated displacement should.
resolution: ReasonCode 600 to 605 (ENROLL_TOKEN_UNKNOWN, _EXPIRED, _USED, CSR_INVALID, PROTO_UNSUPPORTED, PREVIOUS_MACHINE_MISMATCH) carried in the Enroll error's ErrorDetail; HelloAck.fleet_id; ByeReason UNKNOWN_MACHINE and FLEET_MISMATCH; duplicate identity redefined in 03-workflows W2 and 02g (silent takeover; triage only on ping-pong within 10 min with a heartbeat in the last 45 s).

title: Browser terminal attach has no error channel, auth or framing spec, and ADR 0016 names the wrong messages
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/terminal.proto:79-83 AttachClosed{string reason} (free strings "idle_timeout", "session_ended", "agent_offline", "detached") is the only failure signal in AttachTerminalResponse (:86-94); agent-side TermClosed (agent/v1/streams.proto:59-63) uses a different string set ("hub_closed", "agent_shutdown"). terminal.proto:3-6 and docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:226-229 say the browser sends the same messages over a WebSocket. docs/adr/0016-browser-transport.md:34 says the WebSocket carries `TermUp`/`TermDown`, which are agent.v1 types; docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:17-21 and ADR 0018:46-50 forbid hub messages embedding agent wire types.
problem: Over HTTP/2 a failed attach (PERMISSION_DENIED, REASON_CODE_SESSION_NOT_FOUND, machine offline, ROLE_INSUFFICIENT) arrives as a Connect error with ErrorDetail. Over WebSocket there are no trailers, so the browser gets only a free-text reason and no ErrorDetail, and the UI path (the primary attach path) is less informed than the CLI. The endpoint path, subprotocol, how auth is presented (browsers cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket; device auth is still open), the first-frame rule, frame-to-close-code mapping and AttachAck cadence appear in no spec, and the generated TS client cannot cover it. ADR 0016's wire names contradict the hub API.
fix: Add an ErrorDetail error field and an AttachCloseReason enum to AttachClosed (keep the string message). Write a short 'Terminal over WebSocket' section in 02b: path, subprotocol, how a browser authenticates (cookie or first-frame token), binary protobuf frames, first frame must be AttachOpen, close-code mapping, and the ack high-water mark. Fix ADR 0016:34 to AttachTerminalRequest/AttachTerminalResponse.
verify: Confirmed. terminal.proto:79-83 AttachClosed has only a free-text reason ('idle_timeout', 'session_ended', 'agent_offline', 'detached') and no ErrorDetail. terminal.proto:1-6 and 02b:226-229 say the browser sends the same messages over a WebSocket. 02b has no WebSocket section: no URL, subprotocol, auth, first-frame rule or close-code mapping, and open question 3 only covers device auth. ADR 0016:34 says the WebSocket carries TermUp/TermDown, which are agent.v1 types (streams.proto:40), contradicting 02b:17-21. The 256 KiB high-water mark is still 'proposed' (terminal.proto:64).
resolution: AttachClosed already carried reason and ErrorDetail (theme A); 02f now specifies endpoint, subprotocol fleet.attach.v1, ticket as first-frame field (AttachOpen.ticket), Host and Origin checks, binary framing and size limits, ack cadence (32 KiB or 200 ms, 256 KiB high-water), close-code mapping per reason. ADR 0016's TermUp/TermDown wording is corrected in ADR 0019 addendum 13 (accepted ADRs are not rewritten).

title: Enrollment trusts whatever CA the server presents (TOFU), and a lost Enroll response strands the agent
evidence: agent/v1/agent.proto:23-26 (Enroll over server-authenticated TLS with only a token) and :46-48,:71-73 (token sent in EnrollRequest; EnrollResponse supplies the CA chain and `ca_fingerprint` the agent then pins). hub/v1/machine.proto:239-248 (`ca_fingerprint` is 'for the owner to compare'; `enroll_command` is `fleet-agent enroll --hub … --token …` with no fingerprint). docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:117-119 (`fleet-agent enroll --token T [--hub addr]`); docs/adr/0004-agent-connectivity.md:76-81 (fingerprint compared by the owner after the fact); docs/specs/03-workflows.md:120-121 (the impostor defence only applies once the CA is pinned). docs/specs/03-workflows.md:99-106,184-190: the token is burned and the machine row created in one tx; the failure table has no row for a lost response.
problem: Before enrollment the agent holds no trust anchor, so a LAN impostor at the typed or mDNS-found address receives the single-use token, the CSR and the machine facts, and the agent then pins the impostor's CA from its reply. Nothing makes the agent verify the fingerprint the owner sees. Separately, if the EnrollResponse is lost after the token burns, a retry gets 'already used' and the agent never learns its machine_id. A new token creates a second machine, and the first row stays ENROLLED forever. EnrollRequest has `install_id` and the CSR key, but no replay rule uses them.
fix: Put the CA fingerprint into the token or the `enroll_command` (`--ca-sha256 …`). The agent must verify the server chain against it before sending the token or CSR. `EnrollResponse.ca_fingerprint` then becomes a self-check. Define Enroll replay: the same (token hash, install_id, CSR public key) within the TTL returns the same certificate and machine_id. Document both in 02-contracts A1. No proto field is strictly required (`enroll_command` string content and CLI flags); additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: The enrollment token embeds the SHA-256 of the CA and the agent verifies the server chain against it before sending token or CSR (no TOFU); Enroll replay by (token secret hash, install_id, CSR key) returns the stored response with EnrollResponse.replayed. agent.proto, machine.proto (token and enroll_command comments), 02g, 03-workflows W1, 01-agent-capabilities A1.

title: Hub identity material (CA key, fleet_id, account salt, settings_epoch) is absent from the data model and backup, and nothing mints a new settings_epoch on restore
evidence: docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:85-112 (entity table: `enroll_tokens`, `cert_serials` but no CA key, server certificate, `fleet_id`, `account_salt`/`salt_version`, `settings_epoch`). docs/adr/0014-storage-confirmed.md:37 (backup = nightly `VACUUM INTO` of state.db only). agent/v1/agent.proto:75-77,85-87,186-194 and docs/specs/02-contracts.md:233-238 (epoch is 'the incarnation id of the hub's settings store'). docs/specs/03e-settings-and-drift.md:119 ('the restored store has a new settings_epoch'). docs/specs/03-workflows.md:131,323-325 (restore handling covers only unknown goal panes and unknown results).
problem: (1) Where the CA private key, hub server cert, fleet_id and salt live is unspecified. If they are outside state.db a restore on a new host cannot authenticate existing agents. If the salt is lost, machines enrolled afterwards compute different AccountKeys for the same login, silently splitting accounts. A regenerated fleet_id makes every agent refuse the hub. If they are inside state.db the backup contains the CA key and salt and needs protection that nothing states. (2) A restored file carries its old settings_epoch, so the agent still holds (E, 20) against a restored (E, 15) and ignores the hub's settings. That is exactly the case the epoch was meant to fix, and no step mints a new epoch at restore. (3) Agent-held durable state the hub no longer knows is unreconciled: probes in Snapshot.probes, sessions with a FLEET_SESSION_ID, machines enrolled after the backup. (4) If the hub is restored on another host or address, EnrollResponse.hub_addresses (agent.proto:79-80) is the only address list, written once. HelloAck cannot update it, and the server cert SAN policy is undefined.
fix: Add a `hub_identity` entity to 03f (fleet_id, CA cert and key, server cert and SAN list, account_salt and salt_version, settings_epoch, store_incarnation). State that backups include it and are secret. Define `fleetd restore` as minting a fresh settings_epoch and hub_instance_id and setting a reconcile flag. Specify the snapshot diff for agent-known but hub-unknown probes and sessions (adopt or StopProbe). Add `repeated string hub_addresses` to HelloAck. All additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: New hub_identity entity in 03f (fleet_id, CA cert and key, server cert and SANs, account_salt, settings_epoch, hub_addresses) stored inside state.db; backups are secret; fleetd restore mints a new settings_epoch, can re-issue the server cert for a new address and sets a 24 h reconcile flag with a diff table (adopt machines, probes, fleet sessions); HelloAck.hub_addresses added. 02g, 03e restore row.

title: Machine deletion and revocation have no state, cascade or live-connection behaviour
evidence: hub/v1/machine.proto:217-226 (DeleteMachine 'revokes the certificate serials; the next Hello is refused', empty response); hub/v1/service.proto:51; MachineState hub/v1/machine.proto:21-30 has no REVOKED/DELETED, though docs/specs/03-workflows.md:154-156 names DELETED. agent/v1/agent.proto:55-58,274-275 (re-enroll with previous_machine_id so history carries over; BYE_REASON_REVOKED). docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:87 ('permanent until deleted'). hub/v1/device.proto:80 contrasts: RevokeDevice 'takes effect at once, including open Watch streams'.
problem: The only revoke path is Delete, which also forgets the machine. A stolen laptop therefore either keeps its history by not being revoked, or loses it (and `previous_machine` has no row to attach to). 'The next Hello is refused' leaves an already-open Connect, Terminal and SessionLog stream alive, so a compromised machine keeps sending events and receiving commands until it reconnects. The fate of rows that reference the machine is unspecified: running goals, sessions and their logs, probes, the outbox, open attaches, triage items and account bindings.
fix: Add MACHINE_STATE_REVOKED and a revoke action that keeps the row. Make delete the second step, allowed only when revoked. On revoke the hub sends Bye{REVOKED} and closes Connect, Terminal and SessionLog at once. Define the cascade: goals go to a terminal phase, probes fail over, log streams are finalised, outbox rows expire, attaches close. Allow `previous_machine` only for revoked or expired rows. Additive (new enum value, RPC or field).
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: MACHINE_STATE_REVOKED, MachineSpec.revocation, RevokeMachine RPC (row kept, Bye{REVOKED} on the live Connect and closing Terminal, SessionLog and attaches); DeleteMachine only for a revoked machine (MACHINE_NOT_REVOKED); previous_machine only for revoked or expired rows (MACHINE_NOT_REENROLLABLE). Cascade table and re-enroll rule in 02g; 03-workflows state text.

title: Security-relevant agent-side decisions have no permanent audit mapping
evidence: agent/v1/events.proto:252-261 (LocalApprovalDecision with decided_by LOCAL_USER), :246-250 (PolicyChanged), agent/v1/snapshot.proto:305-316 (local drain). docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:97 (`events` retention 1 week) vs :112 (`audit_log` permanent); hub/v1/settings.proto:104-127 (AuditEntry.actor is the original requester, `outcome`/`reason`, free-text `action` and `detail`, no catalog). docs/specs/02-contracts.md:157 (L3).
problem: Who approved or denied a KillWindow or RespawnPane at the machine, who drained a machine locally, and policy-file changes or safe-mode entry live only in the 1-week events table (plus a transient Operation). The permanent audit shows the requester and final status but not the local decider. Audit `action` names are free strings with no catalog, so CSV export and filters will drift.
fix: Define an audit action catalog (enum or documented list) in 02b. Map LocalApprovalDecision, local drain, PolicyChanged and safe-mode entry to AuditEntry rows with actor Principal kind LOCAL_USER. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: 02b "Audit actions" catalogue of every action name; 02g maps LocalApprovalDecision, command refusals (REJECTED_BY_POLICY, LOCAL_DENIED, LOCAL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT), local drain, PolicyChanged and safe mode to permanent AuditEntry rows with actor kind LOCAL_USER; AuditEntry.occurred_time added for agent-clock decisions. Safe mode is read from PolicyInfo.schema_version being empty until an explicit field is added.

title: Docs promise hub-to-agent traces, but Command, Event and Settings carry no trace context
evidence: docs/specs/03e-settings-and-drift.md:134-136 and 03c-goals.md:183-186 (spans `hub.settings.publish` to `agent.settings.merge`, `hub.scheduler.plan` to `hub.command.send` to `agent.start_goal`, `hub.drain` to `agent.drain`); docs/adr/0001-system-architecture.md:60 (OTEL traces from the first version); agent/v1/command.proto:24-84 (Command envelope has no trace field); grep 'trace' in api/: none.
problem: All commands ride one long-lived Connect stream, so per-RPC gRPC metadata cannot propagate a W3C traceparent per command. Without an envelope field the cross-process spans in the workflow docs cannot be linked. Correlation falls back to command_id attributes only.
fix: Add `string traceparent` (W3C) to Command, and to Event or CommandResult for the reverse direction. Document it as optional and capped at 55 bytes. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: New type/v1/trace.proto TraceContext{traceparent, tracestate}; field added to Command.trace, CommandResult.trace, Event.trace and agent Settings.trace (optional, validated and dropped if malformed, 55 and 256 bytes); Operation.trace_id for UI links. Spans in 03c and 03e now name the carrier; 02g.
